summary.text: This briefing examines the integration of gaussian process regression with kolmogorov arnold networks, building on recent research addressing the limitations of exact inference scaling and lack of probabilistic outputs in standard neural architectures (paper:2512.00260, paper:2512.05306). By combining sparse variational Gaussian process inference with the Kolmogorov-Arnold network topology, models achieve quasi-linear computational scaling while propagating uncertainty through deep additive structures (paper:2512.00260, paper:2512.05306). DVF axis scores for this combination are D: 3.0, F: 3.0, and V: 3.0 (dvf:7).

target_user.text: No evidence in the bundle; hypothesis to test: Machine learning researchers and scientific computing practitioners building probabilistic regression models for complex physical or simulation datasets.

jtbd.text: Performing uncertainty-aware regression and flow field reconstruction from sparse measurements while distinguishing aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty.

value_prop.text: Enables scalable Bayesian inference with computational complexity quasi-linear in sample size and provides principled epistemic uncertainty quantification alongside interpretable additive network structures.

riskiest_assumption.text: The lowest feasibility score (F: 3.0) on dvf:7 indicates that integrating sparse variational Gaussian process inference into Kolmogorov-Arnold network topologies may suffer from unstable analytic moment matching or prohibitive scaling bottlenecks when propagating uncertainty through deep additive layers on larger scientific datasets.

mvp.text: Build a technical proof of concept using existing packages to implement a Sparse Variational Gaussian Process Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (SVGP-KAN) on a benchmark regression task, evaluating whether quasi-linear scaling and calibrated uncertainty metrics can be achieved (dvf:7, paper:2512.00260).
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Proposed threshold: test negative log-likelihood and uncertainty calibration error improve by at least 15 percent compared to standard multi-layer perceptrons or exact Gaussian process baselines on regression benchmarks (dvf:7, paper:2512.05306).

kill_criteria.text: Proposed threshold: computational training complexity exceeds $O(N^2)$ scaling as dataset size N increases, violating the quasi-linear efficiency requirement (dvf:7, paper:2512.00260).
Proposed threshold: predictive uncertainty estimates fail to achieve correlation with out-of-distribution error, scoring below 0.5 on held-out anomaly detection tests (dvf:7, paper:2512.05306).

open_source.use: Used to evaluate and calibrate the predictive uncertainty and confidence estimates generated by the probabilistic regression models.

to_build.text: An analytic moment-matching module for propagating sparse variational Gaussian process distributions through the edge-wise univariate functions of the Kolmogorov-Arnold network topology (dvf:7, paper:2512.05306).
